patients.summary: Healthy elementary school teacher who joined the practice at 27 with one prior term delivery and a history of gallstones. Her second pregnancy brought threatened preterm labor at 32 weeks and GBS colonization before an uncomplicated term delivery in 2025; her third ended at 28 weeks in July 2026 with ruptured membranes and preterm labor in an anencephalic pregnancy and a stillbirth.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 27 y/o teacher whose primary care doctor left her old office over the summer. Heard about the membership practice from a coworker. Explained the membership and that her insurance still covers labs, imaging and prescriptions. She signed up online during the call. New patient visit booked 9/12 at 3:45 pm (after school). Sent the records release form so we can get her old chart. Asked her to bring a list of any medicines and her vaccine card.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 y/o woman establishing care. Previous PCP left practice this summer; records release signed, request out.

She feels well and has no complaints today. Teaches second grade, school year just started.

PMH: Gallstones seen on an abdominal ultrasound in spring 2022 at her old office, done after a single bout of upper belly pain that went away by itself. Never saw a surgeon. No pain, nausea or food intolerance since. Otherwise healthy.
PSH: none.
OB/GYN: G1P1. One term vaginal delivery in 2021, no complications in pregnancy or labor. Periods regular. Last Pap 2021 per patient, normal, done at her old office.
Meds: none. Not on contraception; she and her husband are open to another child down the road but not trying.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: Mother had one miscarriage. A second cousin on her mother's side was born with spina bifida. No early heart disease, diabetes or cancer that she knows of.
SH: Married, lives in Springfield with her husband and their child. Never smoked, no vaping. Alcohol a drink or two a month. No drug use. Walks most evenings.

ROS: negative except as above.

Exam: Vitals as recorded. BMI about 24. Well appearing, pleasant. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no RUQ tenderness, Murphy negative, no masses. No edema. Skin without rashes. Mood and affect normal.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 1.

A/P:
1. Establishing care, health maintenance. CBC, CMP, fasting lipids, one-time HIV and hep C screening today. Pap due 2024; will do at her physical next spring. Flu and updated COVID shots offered; she'd rather come back in October once the new COVID vaccine is in.
2. History of gallstones, asymptomatic. No workup needed. Reviewed what biliary pain feels like and when to call.
3. Future pregnancy: start a prenatal vitamin with folic acid a few months before trying. She'll let us know.

Return for annual physical in spring, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Willa, everything from Tuesday's blood work is back and looks good. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and cholesterol are all in the healthy range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do. See you in October for shots.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax from previous PCP office, 41 pages, scanned to chart.

Abstracted:
- Cervical cytology 06/2021: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- Abdominal ultrasound 03/2022: cholelithiasis, otherwise unremarkable; no gallbladder wall thickening.
- Immunizations: childhood series complete per state registry printout; Tdap 2021 during pregnancy; COVID primary series 2021.
- No chronic medications on last med list.

Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Here after school for vaccines. Feels well, no fever. Not pregnant. No prior vaccine reactions.
Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. COVID updated vaccine 0.3 mL IM left deltoid. VIS for both given.
Waited 15 min in the lobby without issue. Registry updated.

documents.title: Starting a vitamin
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! My husband and I have decided to start trying for a second baby sometime this summer. You mentioned the prenatal vitamin last fall. Is there one you'd recommend, or can you send one in so insurance covers it? Thanks!

documents.title: RE: Starting a vitamin
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great news. I sent a prescription prenatal vitamin with 800 mcg of folic acid to your pharmacy, one a day. Starting now is perfect timing. We'll go over anything else at your physical next month, and once you have a positive test let us know and we'll get you set up with obstetrics.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Feels well. Started the prenatal vitamin last month, tolerating it; mild nausea the first week only. Plans to start trying in July after school is out. Cycles regular, LMP 4/2.
No gallbladder symptoms.

Meds: prenatal vitamin daily. NKDA.
SH unchanged: never smoker, rare alcohol, plans to stop once trying.

Exam: Vitals as charted, weight up slightly from fall. Well. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses, no nipple discharge, no axillary nodes. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vaginal mucosa normal, cervix without lesions; Pap collected. Bimanual: uterus normal size, no adnexal masses or tenderness. Extremities no edema.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
1. Preventive care. Pap today (last 2021). CBC, BMP, TSH before pregnancy. Up to date on Tdap (2021) and COVID. Flu in the fall.
2. Preconception. Continue prenatal vitamin. Avoid alcohol once trying. Reviewed the cousin's spina bifida: folic acid at this dose is the standard recommendation and she is taking it. Will refer to OB when pregnant.
3. Hx gallstones: quiet.

RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Pap and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Willa, your Pap came back normal and your blood count, chemistries and thyroid are all normal. Next Pap in three years. Good luck this summer!

documents.title: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning, I took a home test this morning and it's positive! My last period started September 22. What do I do next? Also I still haven't had my flu shot, is it ok to get it while pregnant?

documents.title: RE: Positive test
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Congratulations! Yes, the flu shot is recommended in pregnancy. I booked you a nurse visit Thursday at 3:30 to confirm the test, give the flu shot and send the obstetrics referral. Keep taking your prenatal vitamin.

documents.title: Pregnancy test and flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Urine hCG in office: positive. LMP 9/22/24, about 4 1/2 weeks. Mild fatigue, no bleeding or cramping. Taking prenatal vitamin daily.
Flu vaccine (trivalent, preservative-free) 0.5 mL IM left deltoid, VIS given, tolerated.
OB referral sent to the hospital obstetrics group per PCP; she will get a call for an intake visit around 8 weeks. Reviewed bleeding/severe pain precautions.

documents.title: Referral follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: OB office confirmed referral received. Intake visit scheduled 11/18. Patient aware.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Pharmacy refill request: prenatal vitamin, #90 with 3 refills. Patient is 15 wks, followed by OB. Pended for PCP.
PCP: approved, sent.

conditions.note: Threatened preterm labor at 32 weeks; fFN positive, cervical length 25 mm, 2 cm/50%.

reports.text: Transvaginal ultrasound for cervical length at 32 weeks 0 days. Single live intrauterine pregnancy noted on brief transabdominal survey, cephalic. Cervical length measured three times on transvaginal view; shortest reproducible measurement 25 mm. No funneling seen at rest.

documents.title: Labor and Delivery Triage Record (outside)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
LABOR & DELIVERY TRIAGE — regional hospital obstetrics service
Date of service: 05/04/2025

29 y/o G2P1001 at 32w0d by LMP c/w early US, presenting with contractions. Painful tightening every 5 min for the last 2 hours, getting stronger. No bleeding, no leakage of fluid. Good fetal movement. Prior pregnancy: term SVD, healthy baby, no complications. This pregnancy has gone smoothly; prenatal care with our group since 8 wks.

Meds: prenatal vitamin (folic acid 800 mcg) daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
PMH: none significant. PSH: none.
FH: maternal second cousin with spina bifida; mother with 1 miscarriage.
SH: elementary teacher. Never smoker. No alcohol in pregnancy, occasional before.

VS on arrival: BP 120/78, HR 88, T 37.1 C (98.8 F).
Abd: fundal height 30 cm. Uterus firm with palpable contractions, nontender between them.
SSE: no pooling, no blood; fFN swab collected before any digital exam.
SVE: 2 cm / 50%.
FHT 150, regular.

fFN: positive.
TVUS: cervical length 25 mm.

Assessment: threatened preterm labor, 32 weeks.

Course: monitored on the unit. Contractions spaced out over the next several hours and had stopped by early evening. Repeat cervical check unchanged. Tracing reassuring throughout.

Disposition: home 19:40. Pelvic rest. Preterm labor precautions reviewed; return for regular contractions, bleeding, fluid or decreased movement. Follow up in our clinic this week.

cc: primary care

documents.title: Records received: L&D triage 5/4
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fax from hospital L&D, triage visit 5/4/25. Scanned and routed to PCP. Ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily from OB added to med list as outside prescription.

documents.title: Check-in after L&D visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt per PCP after triage record came in. She is home, no contractions since Sunday evening, baby moving well. Took the rest of the week off from school, OB clinic visit Thursday. Knows when to go back to L&D. Asked her to let us know if she needs a work note beyond what OB gives. Message to PCP.

documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Prenatal visit, 36w1d. G2P1001.

Seen after her triage visit in early May for threatened preterm labor. No further contractions. Denies discharge, fever or urinary symptoms. Active fetal movement.

Meds: PNV daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. NKDA.
Vitals today normal. FHR regular, no decelerations on brief monitoring.
Tdap given 04/07/25 at 28 wks.

GBS: rectovaginal culture collected today. Result 6/4: POSITIVE for group B strep.

Plan: GBS positive — IV penicillin in labor; she is aware and knows to come in early once labor starts or with any rupture of membranes. Weekly visits until delivery. Preterm labor problem can be considered closed at term.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Admitted 06/22/2025, discharged 06/24/2025.

29 y/o G2P1001 at 39w0d admitted in spontaneous labor. GBS positive this pregnancy; penicillin G IV started on admission, more than 4 hours before delivery. Labor progressed without augmentation. Spontaneous vaginal delivery of a vigorous liveborn term infant, to the newborn nursery. Placenta delivered spontaneously, intact. No laceration requiring repair. EBL within normal limits.

Postpartum course uncomplicated. Afebrile. Ambulating, voiding, tolerating diet. Breast and newborn care teaching done.

Discharge diagnoses: term pregnancy, delivered by SVD; GBS carrier, adequately treated in labor. Prior threatened preterm labor at 32 wks, resolved; delivered at term.

Discharge meds: prenatal vitamin daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: OB postpartum visit in 6 weeks. Primary care as needed.

Now G2P2002.

documents.title: Baby update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted to let you know the baby came on the 22nd, right on time, and everyone is home and doing well. Tired but happy. Do I need to see you for anything or just OB for now?

documents.title: RE: Baby update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations to all of you! I read the hospital summary and everything went smoothly. Just OB for now; they'll see you at six weeks. We'll catch up at your physical in the fall. Reach out any time if something comes up, including mood, sleep or feeding questions.

documents.title: Postpartum Visit (outside)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Postpartum visit, 6 weeks after SVD on 6/22. Lochia has stopped. No pain, no urinary or bowel complaints. Sleeping in stretches; good support at home. Edinburgh screen negative.

Vitals normal. Breasts without masses or tenderness. Abdomen soft, uterus not palpable. Perineum healed. Speculum and bimanual normal.

Assessment: normal postpartum course.
Plan: may resume all activity. Continue PNV; may continue iron until bottle is finished. Contraception reviewed; she declines a method for now. Return to primary care for routine care. Annual GYN with us or PCP.

cc: primary care

documents.title: Cancellation
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel tomorrow's physical, parent-teacher meeting at school. Rebooked 10/14 at 3:45.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Nearly 4 months postpartum, second child born 6/22 at term. Back at school since late August. Tired, as expected with an infant, but sleeping in reasonable blocks now. Mood good; husband and her mother are helping. No gallbladder symptoms.

Pregnancy review: L&D triage at 32 wks for contractions with positive fFN and cervix 25 mm, settled with observation. GBS positive at 36 wks, treated in labor. Delivered vaginally at 39 wks without complication. OB postpartum visit normal in August.

Meds: prenatal vitamin daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily (from OB; still taking). NKDA.
No contraception; they'd like to space the next one but aren't strict about it.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Weight down about 2 kg since August, a couple of kilos above her pre-pregnancy weight. Well appearing. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no RUQ tenderness. Ext no edema. Affect bright.

PHQ-9 2. AUDIT-C 1.

A/P:
1. Preventive. Flu and 2025-26 COVID vaccines today. Pap next due 2027. CBC on iron and BMP.
2. Postpartum, doing well. Fine to keep the prenatal vitamin; she can stop the iron once the count is back if she wants.
3. Hx gallstones, asymptomatic.
4. G2P2.

RTC 1 year.

reports.text:
Indication: anatomy survey, 20 weeks 0 days by LMP consistent with first-trimester ultrasound.
Single intrauterine pregnancy. Fetal cardiac activity present. Cephalic.
Cranium: the cranial vault is absent and no cerebral hemispheres are seen above the level of the orbits, consistent with anencephaly. Findings confirmed in multiple planes.
Face: orbits present. Spine: visualized portions without an open defect. Heart: four-chamber view and outflow tracts normal. Abdomen: stomach, kidneys and bladder present; abdominal wall intact. Limbs: four limbs seen.
Biometry other than head measurements consistent with dates.
Amniotic fluid normal. Placenta posterior, no previa. Cervix long and closed on transabdominal view.

documents.title: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Consultation (outside)
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
Maternal-fetal medicine consultation, 05/26/2026. Referred by obstetrics for the detailed anatomy survey.

30 y/o G3P2002 at 20w0d. Two prior term vaginal deliveries. Prior pregnancy with threatened preterm labor at 32 wks and GBS colonization. Taking prenatal vitamin with folic acid 800 mcg daily and ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. NKDA. Family history notable for a maternal second cousin with spina bifida.

Today's ultrasound shows anencephaly (see report). I reviewed the findings with the patient and her husband in detail, including that this is a lethal condition: an affected baby either dies before birth or within hours to days after. We went through all the options for the rest of the pregnancy. She would like to continue the pregnancy and will be followed by her obstetrician with our input. We will see her again as needed.

We also discussed that the chance of a neural tube defect is higher in any future pregnancy and that higher-dose folic acid before conception lowers that chance; we will go over this in detail when the time comes.

Social work contact information given.

cc: obstetrics, primary care

events.reason: rupture of membranes and contractions at 28 weeks

reports.text: Limited bedside ultrasound at 28 weeks 0 days. Single intrauterine pregnancy with known anencephaly. No fetal cardiac activity seen on prolonged interrogation, confirmed by a second examiner. No fetal movement. Placenta posterior.
reports.conclusion: Intrauterine fetal death in a pregnancy with known anencephaly.

documents.title: Labor and Delivery Admission Note (outside)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
L&D ADMISSION — 07/21/2026

30 y/o G3P2002 at 28w0d, pregnancy affected by anencephaly diagnosed on the 20-week scan, here with a gush of fluid about 4 hours ago and contractions every 5 minutes since. Previous pregnancy: threatened preterm labor at 32 wks, GBS colonized, then term SVD. First pregnancy uncomplicated SVD. Both prior deliveries without complication.

She is tearful. She understands the outlook for this baby has been very poor since May; her own concern today is what this means for her body and what her choices are.

Meds: PNV, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. NKDA. No surgeries.
FH: maternal second cousin with spina bifida; mother with a miscarriage.
SH: never smoker; no alcohol in pregnancy. Teacher.

VS stable, afebrile.
SSE: clear fluid pooling, consistent with ROM.
SVE: 3 cm / 80%.
FHTs not obtained by Doppler. Bedside US: no fetal cardiac activity.

A/P: PPROM at 28 wks in active preterm labor; intrauterine fetal demise in a pregnancy with anencephaly.
We talked through what happens next with her and her husband. With membranes ruptured and labor already under way, letting labor continue toward a vaginal delivery carries the least risk to her; a cesarean offers her no benefit and adds surgical risk. Waiting is not advised once membranes have been ruptured for a long time because of infection risk. Comfort measures and pain relief reviewed. She agrees with the plan. Chaplain and bereavement team notified per her wishes.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Admitted 07/21/2026, discharged 07/23/2026.

Diagnoses: preterm premature rupture of membranes with preterm labor at 28 weeks; intrauterine fetal demise; fetal anencephaly.

Course: Labor progressed without augmentation. Vaginal delivery of a stillborn infant with anencephaly that evening. Placenta delivered complete. No laceration needing repair. Bleeding normal. She and her husband spent time with the baby, and memory-making was offered by the bereavement team. Afebrile throughout. Postpartum course uncomplicated; ambulating, voiding, tolerating diet, bleeding light at discharge.

Discharge: home in stable condition. Continue prenatal vitamin and ferrous sulfate. Breast care and supportive measures for milk coming in reviewed. Bereavement resources and support group information given.
Follow-up: OB postpartum visit in 3 to 4 weeks; primary care within 1 to 2 weeks.

Now G3P2102.

cc: primary care

documents.title: Postpartum Visit (outside)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Postpartum visit, 4 weeks after vaginal delivery of a stillborn infant at 28 wks (anencephaly; PPROM with preterm labor).

Bleeding has stopped. No pain. Breasts comfortable. Mood: sad, coping, good support; Edinburgh screen negative. Considering the hospital's bereavement group with her husband.

Vitals normal. Abdomen soft. Pelvic exam normal; uterus normal size, nontender.

Assessment: normal physical recovery.

Future pregnancy counseling: after a pregnancy affected by a neural tube defect, we recommend folic acid 4 mg daily starting at least one month before trying to conceive and continuing through the first trimester, along with a preconception visit at maternal-fetal medicine. She and her husband are not planning another pregnancy at this time; she will let us know and we will prescribe it then. Contraception discussed; she prefers no method for now and understands to use condoms if she wants to avoid pregnancy.

May return to work as she feels ready. Continue prenatal vitamin. Return as needed or for annual GYN care.

cc: primary care
